example.name: adding_a_new_page
example.scenario: The user wants to add a new "Showcase" page to the Sounio website that highlights a scientific visualization example. The page should include a hero section, a description, an interactive visualization (using JavaScript), and a code snippet.
example.user_request: "Add a new showcase page for the visual quantum simulator example."

step.description: Analyze the request and identify required files
step.approach: Determine that a new content file is needed under `hugo/content/showcases/visual-quantum.md` and possibly a new layout or partial for the interactive visualization. Check existing showcase pages for patterns.
step.expected_outcome: List of files to create/modify: content file, maybe a JavaScript asset.

step.approach: Create a new Markdown file with appropriate front matter (title, date, weight). Write the page content, referencing existing assets.
step.analysis: Ensure the front matter matches Hugo's expectations for showcases.

step.approach: Create a new JavaScript file in `hugo/static/js/visual-quantum.js`. Add necessary HTML container and CSS styling. Ensure the visualization is responsive and accessible.
Check if the existing showcase layout (`hugo/layouts/showcases/single.html`) supports the new visualization. If not, extend the layout with a partial or add custom CSS/JS blocks.
Run Hugo locally (if possible) to verify the page renders correctly. Test interactivity, responsiveness, and accessibility. Optimize image and script loading.

example.completion: The new showcase page is live, with proper content, interactive visualization, and meets performance and accessibility standards.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Follow existing Hugo content patterns for consistency.
Separate concerns: content in Markdown, interactivity in JavaScript, styling in CSS.
Always validate with real Hugo build and browser testing.

example.name: improving_accessibility_of_navigation
example.scenario: The navigation menu lacks proper keyboard navigation and screen reader support. The user wants to make the menu fully accessible.
example.user_request: "Improve accessibility of the main navigation menu."

step.approach: Locate the navigation partial (`hugo/layouts/partials/nav.html`). Review the HTML structure and existing CSS/JS.
step.expected_outcome: Understand current flaws: missing ARIA attributes, keyboard traps, etc.

step.approach: Add ARIA roles and labels (aria-label, aria-expanded, aria-controls). Ensure keyboard focus is managed correctly (tabindex, focus states). Implement dropdowns that are operable with keyboard (Enter/Space, arrow keys).
Use axe DevTools or Lighthouse to audit the navigation. Test manually with keyboard-only navigation and screen reader (NVDA/VoiceOver).
Enhance focus styles (outline, background) to meet WCAG contrast requirements. Ensure focus indicators are not removed by CSS reset.

example.completion: The navigation menu is now fully accessible, passes WCAG 2.1 AA, and provides a better experience for keyboard and screen‑reader users.

key_takeaways.takeaway: Accessibility is not just ARIA; also keyboard navigation and visual focus.
Test with real assistive technology whenever possible.
